claims.text: An article has become the way the owner answers people: a page with the sources that stays answered for the next person.
claims.quote: an article has become the way I answer people.

claims.text: Almost every article is written by one model, and a model with a lot of context does more and misses more.
claims.quote: almost every article here is written by one model, and a model with a lot of context does more and misses more.

claims.text: Every article should get a second pass by readers that are not the writer: other models first, then the owner, then the journalists on the desk.
claims.quote: So I want a second pass on every article, by readers that are not the writer.

claims.text: The published criteria are six questions, each answered pass, issues or not checked: facts, voice, claims and limits, conversions, health, people.
claims.quote: Six questions, each answered pass, issues or not checked

claims.text: Not checked is allowed and asked for: a review that checked three things properly is worth more than one that skimmed six.
claims.quote: a review that checked three things properly is worth more than one that skimmed six.

claims.text: A review is one file in the article's own folder, named by its date and reviewer, written once and never edited, about one text of the article identified by a hash.
claims.quote: A review is one file, in the article's own folder of reviews, named by its date and its reviewer. It is written once by its reviewer and never edited.

claims.text: The unit of work is the reviewer, the article and the hash of its text, so a reviewer never gets the same article at the same text twice.
claims.quote: The unit of work is the reviewer, the article and that hash. A reviewer never gets the same article at the same text twice.

claims.text: A reviewer takes its next five articles, newest first, from a status file listing every article's current hash and the reviews it already has.
claims.quote: it takes its next five, newest first, from a status file that lists every article's current hash and the reviews it already has.

claims.text: Before it starts, a reviewer reads its own past reviews and the newsroom's answers, so it does not raise again what was already answered.
claims.quote: Before it starts, it reads its own past reviews and the newsroom's answers to them, so it does not raise again what has already been answered.

claims.text: A pull request touching only review files is the best fit today for an agent from another vendor: attributable, reviewable and checkable before merge.
claims.quote: For an agent from another vendor this is the best fit today: it is attributable, it is reviewable

claims.text: Later, a review can arrive by the editor's channel's append lane, sent without an account and sealed so only the newsroom can read it.
claims.quote: a reviewer can send without an account, sealed so that only the newsroom can read it.

claims.text: Every finding gets an answer in a status file only the newsroom writes: fixed with the version, declined with the reason, or open.
claims.quote: A finding with no answer is just a complaint.

claims.text: Findings are worked through in the daily pass with the usual rule: what is cheap to undo is fixed and released, and anything that changes an argument goes to the owner.
claims.quote: what is cheap to undo is fixed and released, and anything that changes an argument goes to me.

claims.text: Every article page now has a Reviews section after the threads: who reviewed it, when, at which version, the verdict, and how many findings were fixed, declined or open.
claims.quote: Every article page now has a Reviews section, after the threads

claims.text: This is not a comments section; it is comments on the record, by someone who said who they are, against criteria everyone can read, kept with the article.
claims.quote: This is comments on the record: a review by someone who said who they are, against criteria everyone can read, kept with the article.

claims.text: The owner's own reading uses the same file: an approval by the editor at that version is the sign-off the editor's channel proposed.
claims.quote: When I have read an article and it is right, that is a review: an approval, by the editor, at that version

claims.text: The most interesting part is that it works backwards in time: a note on the record a year later saying I got this wrong, or this came true.
claims.quote: And it works backwards in time, which I think is the most interesting part.

claims.text: The next step is signed readers with a key of their own, who confirm or dispute an article and whose reviews count because they are signed.
claims.quote: signed readers, with a key of their own, who confirm or dispute an article, agree or disagree with it, and whose reviews count because they are signed.

claims.text: The first reviewer was another model from the same vendor as the writer, given the criteria and the five newest articles.
claims.quote: The first reviewer was another model, from the same vendor as the one that writes the articles

claims.text: The first run took about nineteen minutes and wrote five records.
claims.quote: It took about nineteen minutes and wrote five records.

claims.text: One article had no findings; the other four had 18 between them, 4 medium and 14 low, none high.
claims.quote: The other four had 18 between them: 4 medium and 14 low, none high.

claims.text: The medium findings were real: a quote attributed to Google linked to coverage that did not carry it, and Mozilla's latest audited statements are for 2024, not 2023.
claims.quote: A quote attributed to Google linked to coverage that did not carry it; Mozilla's latest audited statements are for 2024, not 2023

claims.text: riskmandate.ai's front page says Enforced in real time while an article says RiskMandate is never in the request path, without saying how the two fit.
claims.quote: says RiskMandate is never in the request path, without saying how the two fit.

claims.text: The reviewer counted curl's 239 vulnerabilities again and got the same 49, and reproduced the CVE counts from NVD's API exactly.
claims.quote: It counted curl's 239 vulnerabilities again and got the same 49

claims.text: Every finding was checked and fixed in the same release that published the article, so those reviews now show as reviews of an earlier text.
claims.quote: Every finding was checked and fixed in the same release that published this article

claims.text: The reviewer also reviewed the criteria unasked, and its points went into version 1.1.
claims.quote: It also reviewed the criteria, unasked, and its points went straight into version 1.1

claims.text: Review does not make an article right; it makes what was checked and what was found visible.
claims.quote: Review does not make an article right. It makes what was checked, and what was found, visible.

claims.text: One reviewer, one batch so far: five articles by one model, with criteria at version 1.1 that will keep changing.
claims.quote: One reviewer, one batch so far. Five articles, by one model

claims.text: Reviewers are models and models make mistakes; a finding is a claim for the newsroom to check, not a verdict.
claims.quote: Reviewers are models, and models make mistakes. A finding is a claim for the newsroom to check, not a verdict.

claims.text: A hash is not a signature: it says which text was reviewed, not who reviewed it, so records are attributed by who sent them until reviewers sign.
claims.quote: A hash is not a signature. It says which text was reviewed, not who reviewed it

claims.text: Nothing reviews the reviewers yet; if two disagree the newsroom answers both and the owner decides.
claims.quote: Nothing reviews the reviewers yet. If two reviewers disagree, the newsroom answers both, and I decide.

claims.text: Signed readers are a proposal, not built.
claims.quote: Signed readers are a proposal.
